summary: The base independently reproduced both reported LlamaForCausalLM startup crashes after GPU weight loading. The exact candidate rejects both auto-filled and explicit multi-layer EAGLE configurations during argument resolution with a clear ValueError, an outcome explicitly allowed by the original issue. Focused regression and boundary tests pass, and ordinary non-multi-layer Llama EAGLE behavior remains unchanged.

tests.what_was_measured: The target loaded on gfx950 as LlamaForCausalLM, then startup reproduced the reported invariant assertion with draft tokens 8 and steps 5.
The target loaded on gfx950, passed the invariant, then reproduced the reported unexpected draft_model_idx keyword passed to LlamaForCausalLM.
Three candidate tests passed: early Llama rejection, unchanged ordinary Llama EAGLE auto-fill (5,4,8), and unchanged MiMoV2 embedded-MTP resolution (3,1,4).

tests.command: the two base launch commands repeated at exact candidate commit on ports 38673 and 38674
tests.what_was_measured: Both auto-fill and explicit-tuple paths raised the intended ValueError during argument resolution, with no weight-load marker, assertion, or constructor TypeError.
227 tests and 44 subtests passed; two unrelated context-parallel tests failed because the prepared HIP platform explicitly rejects prefill CP.

gpu_evidence: Both failing-before serving runs loaded the deterministic Llama weights on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 GPU before reaching the reported failures.
remaining_limitations: The review environment was AMD gfx950 with ROCm 7.2 and Torch 2.11.0, not the reporter's NVIDIA CUDA environment.

The deterministic two-layer random Llama fixture validates startup, argument resolution, GPU model loading, and constructor dispatch only; it does not validate TinyLlama semantic accuracy or full-model behavior.
No supported embedded-MTP checkpoint weights were available, so multi-layer EAGLE generation on such an architecture was not exercised; only its independent MiMoV2 configuration boundary was tested.
The full server-argument module has two unrelated existing failures on HIP where prefill context parallelism is intentionally rejected.
